subject: jet hand dryer
title: What If You Always Used Jet Hand Dryers?

scenes.text: What if you always dried your hands with a jet dryer? Your hands aren't the problem.
Hands are rarely perfectly clean after washing, and jet dryers blast the leftover water off at high speed.
Leeds scientists coated hands with harmless bacteria and measured the air afterwards.
Near jet dryers, airborne bacteria were 27 times higher than near paper towels.
Some still hung in the air fifteen minutes later, for the next person to breathe.
In hospital toilets, floors had at least five times more bacteria. The paper towel wins, at least for the room.

description:
What if you always used jet air hand dryers? A University of Leeds study found airborne bacteria 27 times higher around jet dryers than around paper towels, with some still in the air 15 minutes later.
A follow-up in hospital toilets found at least five times more bacteria on floors when jet dryers were used. Both studies were funded by the paper towel industry's trade group.
